summary: All 22 tests in reopen-cancelled-wp.test.ts pass (exceeds 18-test minimum).
Full regression suite: 96 test files, 2891 tests, 0 failures — no regressions.
Verified the IN_PROGRESS cascade reblock test (test #22) is valid: propagateDependencyReblock filters on !isTerminalStatus && !== BLOCKED, which correctly catches IN_PROGRESS dependents.

comments.note: The WP-002 deliverables list includes a guard test for BLOCKED status (not CANCELLED), but no explicit test for that case exists. The implementation does reject BLOCKED (it rejects anything !== CANCELLED), so behaviour is correct. Since the AC metric is 18-test minimum (exceeded at 22) not a per-deliverable checklist, this does not block QA pass. Recommend adding a BLOCKED-status guard test in a follow-up.

Status guard tests (READY/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETE) involve disk reads inside updateWorkPackageWithSync but return data unchanged. The write-back of identical values is a side effect worth noting: the AC says 'no state mutation' which holds semantically (values unchanged), but a lock + file write still occurs. Implementation is correct and consistent with updateWorkPackageStatus pattern.

propagateDependencyReblock has an optimistic pre-check that skips the batch update when no ACTION_STATUSES dependents exist. This is a read-then-write race window, but it is documented in the source and is a best-effort optimisation — worst case is a WP transitions to READY/IN_PROGRESS between the pre-check and the batch call, which is benign (it would just not be caught until the next status transition). No test covers this race; it is an acceptable concurrency edge case.

comments.note: The cascade reblock tests in the READY and IN_PROGRESS scenarios (reopen-cancelled-wp.test.ts) create WP-002 with pipelines: [] via makeWpDetail defaults. This means autoCancelActivePipelines is invoked but finds nothing to cancel. The auto-cancel side-effect is NOT verified within the reopenCancelledWp end-to-end path. This is acceptable because propagateDependencyReblock is tested in isolation (work-package.test.ts:1768, 1936) with full pipeline assertions. However, the test could be made more self-documenting with an inline comment pointing readers to the propagateDependencyReblock test suite for auto-cancel coverage.

The status-guard tests (READY/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETE, reopen-cancelled-wp.test.ts lines ~104–175) write disk state before calling the function, which is correct. However, the notCancelledStatus pattern in the implementation means updateWorkPackageWithSync reads, acquires the lock, and writes back unchanged values before returning the error. This is a read-lock-write no-op for the error path — semantically correct and QA-accepted, but a pre-read guard before entering the atomic sync (mirroring the PM-only guard) would be cleaner. Not a test issue; flagged for future implementation refinement.

[documentation-forward] The IN_PROGRESS cascade reblock test ('blocks downstream IN_PROGRESS dependents after reopening the CANCELLED WP') does not include a comment explaining that pipeline auto-cancel behaviour is covered by the propagateDependencyReblock test suite in work-package.test.ts. A single inline comment would close the coverage-story gap for future contributors and prevent unnecessary confusion during audits.

No explicit guard test for BLOCKED-status WP (QA-noted coverage gap). Implementation correctly rejects BLOCKED (anything !== CANCELLED is rejected), and the 22-test threshold is exceeded. Recommend adding a BLOCKED guard test in a follow-up to make the deliverables list exhaustively covered.
